name: Pottery
overview: Scripture uses pottery as a vivid illustration of God's sovereign authority and creative power. The imagery of the potter shaping clay, as seen in Isaiah and Jeremiah, underscores our dependence on God as the Master Craftsman who can reshape and restore us according to His will. Pottery also symbolizes human weakness and fragility, reflected in Daniel's vision where the feet of the statue are partly made of potter's clay, representing a mixture of strength and vulnerability. Additionally, the purchase of the potter's field for burying strangers, recorded in Matthew, connects pottery with God's provision even in death, emphasizing His care for the marginalized.
